findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() will not compile
findings.body: `authenticate()` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only method defined is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` (added in this PR), and no no-arg overload exists in `UsernamePasswordForm`, `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator` or `AbstractFormAuthenticator`. The services module therefore fails to compile. The intended call is presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires a non-null user, disabling conditional passkeys on the anonymous login page
findings.body: `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns true only when `user != null`. It replaces the previous checks which deliberately filled the WebAuthn conditional-UI data when `context.getUser() == null` (the normal, ID-less login). As a result, on a fresh login (no user in the context) `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` is no longer invoked at line 115, so the login page gets no challenge/RP-ID/conditional-UI attributes and discoverable-key (passkey) autofill/auto-login no longer works at all for first-time authentication. This contradicts the feature's main flow and the existing tests that assert `//form[@id='webauth']` and autocomplete `"username webauthn"` on the initial login page. The condition should not require a non-null user (it most likely should just be `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled()`).

findings.title: Error-challenge no longer re-fills passkey data when no user is established
findings.body: The `challenge(context, error, field)` override previously filled the WebAuthn conditional-UI data when `context.getUser() == null`; it now does it only when the user is non-null (`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` requires `user != null`). Consequently, when an unauthenticated login attempt fails (e.g. unknown username, empty password), the re-rendered login form loses all passkey attributes and the user can no longer authenticate with a passkey from that error page — a regression of the previously working behaviour covered by existing tests (e.g. PasskeysUsernameFormTest.passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey asserts the webauthn autocomplete after an invalid-user error).

findings.title: Test named reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey actually only disables realm passkeys
findings.body: `reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey` sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(FALSE)`, i.e. it verifies that the passkey form is hidden when the realm does not have passkeys enabled — not that it is hidden for a user who has no passkey credential. Since `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` only checks the realm/feature flag and never whether the user owns a WebAuthn credential, a passkeys-enabled realm will now render the passkey option during re-authentication for users with no (or no discoverable) passkey, and `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators()` returns false so no `allowCredentials` is sent, making the option unusable for such users. There is no test covering that combination, and the misleading test name hides the gap.
